text: In a quiet town a shoemaker and his wife live together. They work hard every day, but they do not sell enough shoes. The store is old and has many problems. The windows are broken, and the sinks leak.

One cold evening, the shoemaker looks at the last piece of leather on his workbench and sighs. "This is all we have left," he said. "Enough leather to make one last pair of shoes." He cuts the leather for the last pair of shoes, and puts it on his desk.
Then he goes to bed, but he cannot fall asleep because he feels nervous. The shoemaker is scared about the future.

text: Making a to-do list helps the shoemaker make a plan and get the rest he needs.
The shoemaker gets up quietly and makes a short to-do list. After he writes everything down, he sees that he can do the tasks. He feels less nervous.
Then he takes a deep breath and goes to bed.

When he wakes up the next morning, something surprising happens. When the shoemaker enters his workshop, he sees a pair of shoes already made. They are the most beautiful pair the shoemaker and his wife have ever seen.
A customer comes in that day and pays lots of money for the shoes. The customer also says how beautiful they are.

text: The shoemaker's wife makes small coats, scarves, and mittens. The shoemaker makes 2 pairs of elf-sized shoes and writes a note to thank them. He tells the elves they do not need to help anymore and can go on their own adventures.

That night, they put the gifts out and hide. When the elves come, they see the gifts. Slowly, they put on the clothes and they smile. They dance, spin in circles, and laugh with joy. They shout tiny "thank you"s.
The shoemaker never sees the elves again, but always remembers the help they gave him.

From then on, the shoemaker's business grows strong not only because of his skill, but because of his thankfulness and kindness. And every time he makes a new pair of shoes, he remembers how the smallest helpers can make the biggest difference.
